{"mode":"iff","restated":"∃ (family : Finset FiniteGraph) (c C : ℝ), family.Nonempty ∧ (∀ forbidden ∈ family, forbidden.graph.Connected ∧ forbidden.graph.IsBipartite ∧ ¬ forbidden.graph.IsAcyclic) ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ UniformMemberLower family c ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (host : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), FamilyFree family host → (host.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ^ 16 ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ 21) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (familyExtremal family n : ℝ) ^ 16 ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ 21) ∧ ¬ IsCompactFamily family ∧ ¬ CompactnessConjectureStatement","proof":"constructor
· rintro ⟨f, c, C, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, -, -, h8, h9⟩
  exact ⟨f, c, C, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8, h9⟩
· rintro ⟨f, c, C, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8, h9⟩
  exact ⟨f, c, C, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, by norm_num, by norm_num, h8, h9⟩","english":"There is a nonempty finite family of connected, bipartite, non-acyclic (so cyclic) forbidden graphs and constants c, C > 0 such that: every member H has ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^(4/3) eventually; every family-free graph on n vertices has e^16 ≤ C·n^21, and likewise the family's extremal number satisfies ex(n,F)^16 ≤ C·n^21 for all n; the family is not compact (no member's extremal number is eventually bounded by a constant multiple of the family's); and the compactness conjecture fails.","why_clearer":"It removes the two trivially true numeric conjuncts (0 < 1/48 and 21/16 = 4/3 − 1/48), which are only bookkeeping for the exponent 4/3 − 1/48, so the real content is easier to see."}

parsed.restated: ∃ (family : Finset FiniteGraph) (c C : ℝ), family.Nonempty ∧ (∀ forbidden ∈ family, forbidden.graph.Connected ∧ forbidden.graph.IsBipartite ∧ ¬ forbidden.graph.IsAcyclic) ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧ UniformMemberLower family c ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (host : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), FamilyFree family host → (host.edgeFinset.card : ℝ) ^ 16 ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ 21) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (familyExtremal family n : ℝ) ^ 16 ≤ C * (n : ℝ) ^ 21) ∧ ¬ IsCompactFamily family ∧ ¬ CompactnessConjectureStatement
parsed.proof:
constructor
· rintro ⟨f, c, C, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, -, -, h8, h9⟩
  exact ⟨f, c, C, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8, h9⟩
· rintro ⟨f, c, C, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8, h9⟩
  exact ⟨f, c, C, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, by norm_num, by norm_num, h8, h9⟩
parsed.english: There is a nonempty finite family of connected, bipartite, non-acyclic (so cyclic) forbidden graphs and constants c, C > 0 such that: every member H has ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^(4/3) eventually; every family-free graph on n vertices has e^16 ≤ C·n^21, and likewise the family's extremal number satisfies ex(n,F)^16 ≤ C·n^21 for all n; the family is not compact (no member's extremal number is eventually bounded by a constant multiple of the family's); and the compactness conjecture fails.
parsed.why_clearer: It removes the two trivially true numeric conjuncts (0 < 1/48 and 21/16 = 4/3 − 1/48), which are only bookkeeping for the exponent 4/3 − 1/48, so the real content is easier to see.
